items.title: Concentration With Applied Thought, With Only Sustained Thought, and With Neither

items.zh: 復次，云何有尋有伺三摩地？謂三摩地尋伺相應。云何無尋唯伺三摩地？謂三摩地唯伺相應。大梵修已、為大梵王。云何無尋無伺三摩地？謂三摩地尋伺二種俱不相應。修習此故，生次上地乃至有頂。唯除無漏諸三摩地。
items.en: Furthermore, what is the concentration with applied and sustained thought? A concentration associated with applied and sustained thought. What is the concentration with only sustained thought? A concentration associated only with sustained thought — the Great Brahmā, having cultivated it, becomes the Great Brahmā King. What is the concentration with neither applied nor sustained thought? A concentration associated with neither; by cultivating it one is reborn in the successively higher grounds up to the peak of existence. Only the uncontaminated concentrations are excepted.

items.zh: 云何無尋無伺三摩地相？謂於尋伺心生棄捨，唯由一味，於內所緣而作勝解，又唯一味平等顯現。
items.en: What is the mark of the concentration with neither applied nor sustained thought? The mind gives rise to a casting-off of applied and sustained thought; by a single flavour alone it generates conviction towards the inner object, and only that single flavour appears, level and even.

items.zh: 復次，云何小三摩地？謂或由所緣故小，觀少色故。或由作意故小，小信、小欲、小勝解故。云何大三摩地？謂或由所緣故大。觀多色故，而非無邊無際觀諸色故。或由作意故大，上信、上欲、上勝解故，而非無邊無際信、欲、勝解故。云何無量三摩地？謂或由所緣故無量，無邊無際觀諸色故。或由作意故無量，無邊無際信、欲、勝解故。
items.en: Further, what is small concentration? It is small either because of its object, since it observes little form; or because of its attention, since its faith, aspiration, and conviction are small. What is great concentration? It is great either because of its object, since it observes much form, though not observing forms without limit or boundary; or because of its attention, since its faith, aspiration, and conviction are superior, though not without limit or boundary. What is immeasurable concentration? It is immeasurable either because of its object, since it observes forms without limit or boundary; or because of its attention, since its faith, aspiration, and conviction are without limit or boundary.

items.title: The Great-Mind Concentration: Contemplating the Light of the Gods

items.zh: 此中大心三摩地者，謂於一樹下，想諸天光而生勝解，乃至廣說。無量三摩地者，謂四無量。云何於一樹下想諸天光而生勝解？謂於欲界極厭壞已，得初靜慮；為令此定善清淨故，更修方便。又聞諸天身帶光明，便思惟彼身光明相，遍一樹下、乃至大地、大海邊際，發生勝解。
items.en: Here the great-mind concentration is: under a single tree, contemplating the light of the gods and generating conviction, and so on at length. The immeasurable concentration is the four immeasurables. How does one, under a single tree, contemplate the gods' light and generate conviction? Having thoroughly wearied of the desire realm and attained the first dhyāna, in order to make this concentration well purified he further cultivates the means; and having heard that the gods' bodies carry light, he contemplates the mark of that bodily light spreading beneath a single tree, and on to the bounds of the great earth and the great ocean, generating conviction.

items.zh: 由三摩地後後轉增有差別故，令所生起而有差別。云何作意得成唯二？謂隨勝解分齊施設作意故。云何作意唯二為緣，修成唯二？謂即由此作意力故，施設所修定有差別，圓滿清淨轉增勝故。云何以修唯二為緣，行成唯二？謂如如善修定轉增勝，如是如是施設所感生有差別。云何以行唯二為緣，補特伽羅建立唯二？謂此因緣所生有情，施設高下勝劣差別。
items.en: Because concentration grows progressively and so differs, what it produces also differs. How does attention come to be only twofold? Because attention is designated according to the extent of conviction. How is cultivation, with only twofold attention as its condition, accomplished as only twofold? Because, by the power of this attention, the concentration cultivated is designated as differing, as it grows ever more complete, pure, and excellent. How is conduct, with only twofold cultivation as its condition, accomplished as only twofold? Because the better concentration is cultivated and the more it grows, the more the births it brings about are designated as differing. How is the establishment of persons, with only twofold conduct as its condition, only twofold? Because beings born from these causes are designated as differing in high and low, superior and inferior.

items.zh: 問：初二靜慮諸天光明有何差別？答：如末尼珠，外有光明，內無光明。初靜慮身亦復如是。外放光明，內則不爾。譬如明燈，外發光明，內自照了。第二靜慮身亦如是，若內若外俱有光明。是故經說：彼地已上唯一種身，非於下地。
items.en: Question: what is the difference between the light of the first- and second-dhyāna gods? Answer: like a maṇi-jewel, which has light outside but none within — so too the first-dhyāna body radiates light outward but not within. Like a bright lamp, which sends light outward and also illumines itself within — so too the second-dhyāna body has light both within and without. Therefore the sūtra says: from that ground upwards there is only one kind of body, unlike the lower grounds.

items.title: The Four Immeasurables: Loving-Kindness, Compassion, Sympathetic Joy, and Equanimity

items.zh: 復次，云何建立四無量定？謂諸有情有三品故。一者、無苦無樂，二者、有苦，三者、有樂。如其次第，欲與其樂、欲令離苦、欲令其樂永不相離。於彼作意有四種故，如其次第，建立四種。謂由與樂作意故、拔苦作意故、樂不相離隨喜作意故，建立前三。即於此三欲與樂等，為欲令彼不樂思慕不染污作意故，瞋恚不染污作意故，貪欲不染污作意故，建立於捨。
items.en: Furthermore, how are the four immeasurable concentrations established? Because beings are of three kinds: those without suffering or pleasure, those with suffering, and those with pleasure. In that order, one wishes to give them happiness, wishes to free them from suffering, and wishes their happiness never to part from them. Because attention towards them is fourfold, four are established in order: by the attention of giving happiness, the attention of removing suffering, and the attention of rejoicing that their happiness not part, the first three are established. And towards these same three — wishing to give happiness and so on — by the undefiled attention [freeing them] from non-delight and longing, the undefiled attention [freeing them] from ill-will, and the undefiled attention [freeing them] from craving, equanimity is established.

items.zh: 經言：以慈俱心，乃至廣說。
items.en: The sūtra says, 'With a mind accompanied by loving-kindness', and so on at length.

items.title: Reading the Sūtra's Loving-Kindness Formula, Term by Term

items.zh: 現前饒益，故名慈俱。饒益相故，名慈善友。其饒益相略有二種。一、欲利益，二、欲安樂。此二種相，一切無量之所顯示。無怨者，離惡意樂故。無敵者，離現乖諍故。無惱害者，離不饒益事故。
items.en: Because it brings benefit in actual deed, it is called "accompanied by loving-kindness." Because it is the mark of benefiting, it is called "a good friend of loving-kindness." Its mark of benefiting is, in brief, of two kinds: wishing to benefit, and wishing to give ease. These two marks are what all the immeasurables display. "Without enmity" means free of ill-willed intent. "Without hostility" means free of present quarrel. "Without harm" means free of un-benefiting deeds.

items.zh: 廣者，所緣廣大故。大者，利益安樂思惟最勝故。無量者，果無量故。如四大河，眾流雜處。善修習者，極純熟故。設有問言：慈俱等心有何等相？故次答言：勝解遍滿，具足而住。勝解遍滿者，增上意樂勝解周普義。具足者，圓滿清白故。住者，所修觀行日夜專注，時專注故。
items.en: "Vast" means the object is vast. "Great" means the thought of benefit-and-ease is supreme. "Immeasurable" means the fruit is immeasurable — like the four great rivers, whose many streams mingle together. "Well-cultivated" means utterly ripened. Should someone ask, "what are the marks of the mind accompanied by loving-kindness and the rest?" the answer follows: "resolved, pervading, complete, and abiding." "Resolved and pervading" means a heightened resolve that reaches all-round; "complete" means perfect and pure; "abiding" means the practice is sustained day and night, moment by moment.

items.zh: 問：如經言：善修習慈，極於遍淨，乃至廣說。此何密意？答：第三靜慮，於諸樂中其樂最勝，憶念此樂修習慈心，慈最第一，故說修慈極於遍淨。
items.en: Question: As the sūtra says, 'Loving-kindness well cultivated culminates in the Pure Universal heaven,' and so on at length. What is the hidden intention here? Answer: In the third dhyāna, the bliss is the highest of all bliss. Recalling this bliss, one cultivates the mind of loving-kindness, and loving-kindness is foremost; so it is said that the cultivation of loving-kindness culminates in the Pure Universal heaven.

blocks.text: Today's reading describes three kinds of concentration by the presence of thought, then a striking "great-mind concentration" based on the light of the gods, and then the **four immeasurables**, explaining the sūtra formula for loving-kindness word by word. If you practise loving-kindness meditation, this is its classical commentary.

Concentration may be with applied and sustained thought, with only sustained thought, or with neither. Cultivating the last leads to rebirth "in the successively higher grounds up to the peak", except when it is uncontaminated, in which case it leads beyond. Venerable Miào Jìng on the thought-free concentration's mark, "conviction towards the inner object": one first sees how applied thought agitates the mind; only when it is gone does the single object stand clear.

Having attained the first dhyāna and heard that the gods' bodies shine, one imagines their light and extends it. The light of first-dhyāna gods is "like a maṇi-jewel, which has light outside but none within"; second-dhyāna gods are "like a bright lamp", light within and without. Venerable Miào Jìng's example of "one body, different perceptions": when the gods of the Radiant Light heaven see the fire that ends an eon, some are afraid and some are not.

"Because beings are of three kinds: those without suffering or pleasure, those with suffering, and those with pleasure." Towards the first one wishes happiness (**loving-kindness**, 慈); towards the second, freedom from suffering (**compassion**, 悲); towards the third, that their happiness not be lost (**sympathetic joy**, 喜); and towards all, **equanimity** (捨), without craving or aversion.
Venerable Miào Jìng gives equanimity a special place: "Love, compassion, and joy are worldly wholesome; equanimity is transcendent Dharma, the noble path." Without it, love becomes attachment.

subs.head: The loving-kindness formula, word by word

blocks.text: The sūtra formula reads: "with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, without enmity, without hostility, without harm, vast, great, immeasurable, well cultivated, pervading one direction … all directions". The treatise explains each term. Master Cháng Bǎi maps "without enmity, without hostility, without harm" onto the three kinds of action: no ill intent in mind, no quarrel in speech, no harm by the body.

Well-cultivated loving-kindness has benefits. Master Cháng Bǎi lists fifteen from an *Avataṃsaka* commentary: sleeping in peace, waking in peace, protection by gods and people, no nightmares, waking glad, and more.

The immeasurables, Venerable Miào Jìng notes, are cultivated "together with the awakening factors": with mindfulness, investigation, energy, joy, tranquillity, concentration, and equanimity. Loving-kindness is not only a feeling to generate; it is a concentration to develop and a path factor to integrate.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what results from cultivating the concentration with neither applied nor sustained thought?
options: rebirth in successively higher grounds up to the peak — the uncontaminated concentrations excepted
quiz.why: "A concentration associated with neither; by cultivating it one is reborn in the successively higher grounds up to the peak of existence. Only the uncontaminated concentrations are excepted." Master Cháng Bǎi: the uncontaminated no longer circulate in saṃsāra.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how is the great-mind concentration cultivated?
options: after wearying of the desire realm and attaining the first dhyāna, hearing that gods' bodies shine, one imagines their light under a tree, spreading to the bounds of earth and sea
quiz.why: "Having thoroughly wearied of the desire realm and attained the first dhyāna … having heard that the gods' bodies carry light, he contemplates the mark of that bodily light spreading beneath a single tree, and on to the bounds of the great earth and the great ocean." Venerable Miào Jìng: first weary, then break down — and you leave the desire realm.

quiz.q: How does the light of first-dhyāna gods differ from second-dhyāna gods?
options: the first-dhyāna body is like a maṇi-jewel, light outside only; the second like a lamp, light within and without
quiz.why: "Like a maṇi-jewel, which has light outside but none within — so too the first-dhyāna body … Like a bright lamp, which sends light outward and also illumines itself within — so too the second-dhyāna body." Master Cháng Bǎi: the light grows vaster in the third and fourth.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, on what basis are the four immeasurables established?
options: beings are of three kinds — neither, suffering, happy; one wishes the first happiness, the second freedom from suffering, the third unbroken happiness; equanimity is set on these with undefiled attention
quiz.why: "Because beings are of three kinds: those without suffering or pleasure, those with suffering, and those with pleasure. In that order, one wishes to give them happiness, wishes to free them from suffering, and wishes their happiness never to part." Venerable Miào Jìng: the neutral ones are dull and confused.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng say equanimity differs from the other three immeasurables?
options: love, compassion, joy are worldly good; equanimity is transcendent, the noble path — without it, it isn't the bodhisattva way
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Love, compassion, and joy are worldly wholesome; equanimity is transcendent Dharma — the noble path." "With love, compassion, and joy but no equanimity, it isn't the bodhisattva path — just ordinary goodness." Equanimity teaches beings to end greed, hatred, and delusion.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi map "without enmity, without hostility, without harm" onto the three kinds of action?
options: without enmity — mind (free of ill intent); without hostility — speech (no quarrels); without harm — body
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Without hostility — no enmity in speech, not opposing or quarreling with beings." The text: "'Without enmity' means free of ill-willed intent. 'Without hostility' means free of present quarrel. 'Without harm' means free of un-benefiting deeds."

quiz.q: On well-cultivated loving-kindness, how many benefits does Master Cháng Bǎi list from the Avataṃsaka commentary?
options: fifteen — sleeping in peace, waking in peace, protected by gods and people, no nightmares, waking glad, not swept away by water, and so on
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Cultivating loving-kindness has fifteen benefits: 1. sleeping peacefully, 2. waking peacefully, 3. protected by gods, 4. by people, 5. no bad dreams, 6. always joyful on waking, 7. water cannot sweep one away …" The text: "'Well-cultivated' means utterly ripened."
